summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Daily combination pills (21 active hormonal + 7 ferrous fumarate pills) contain synthetic Progestogens + Estrogens, inhibiting ovulation by negative feedback on LH/FSH and altering cervical mucus. Long-acting options: Depo-Provera (IM injection every 3 months) and Norplant (6 subdermal levonorgestrel rods, effective for 5 years). Emergency Contraception (Unwanted-72 / Levonorgestrel 1.5 mg) administered within 72 hours of unprotected intercourse.

conceptBreakdown.content:
### 5.1 Combined Oral Contraceptive Pills (COCPs)
- **Regimen (21 + 7 Schedule)**: Taken daily for $21\text{ consecutive days}$ starting within the first 5 days of the menstrual cycle, followed by a $7\text{-day}$ pill-free (or iron placebo) interval during which withdrawal bleeding occurs.
- **Tripartite Physiological Mechanism**:
  1. **Inhibition of Ovulation**: Sustained blood levels of progestogen and estrogen exert continuous negative feedback on hypothalamic GnRH and anterior pituitary FSH/LH secretion, abolishing the mid-cycle LH surge.
  2. **Cervical Mucus Thickening**: Progestogens turn cervical mucus thick, tenacious, and cellular, forming an impassable barrier to sperm ascent.
  3. **Endometrial Desynchronization**: Prevents normal secretory maturation of the endometrium, rendering it atrophic and unreceptive to blastocyst implantation.

### 5.2 Injectables & Subdermal Implants

```
                      LONG-ACTING REVERSIBLE CONTRACEPTION
                      
   1. DEPO-PROVERA (DMPA): Depot Medroxyprogesterone Acetate (150 mg IM injection).
      └── Provides highly effective contraception for 3 MONTHS per dose.
      
   2. NORPLANT / IMPLANON: Subdermal matchstick-sized silastic capsules.
      └── Placed under upper arm skin; releases Levonorgestrel continuously for up to 5 YEARS.
```

### 5.3 Emergency Contraception Protocol
- **Definition**: Interventions used to prevent pregnancy after unprotected sexual intercourse, contraceptive failure (e.g., condom breakage), or sexual assault.
- **Time Window**: Must be administered **within 72 hours (3 days)** of unprotected coitus.
- **Modalities**:
  1. **Levonorgestrel (1.5 mg single dose / Unwanted-72, i-Pill)**: High-dose progestin that delays or prevents follicular rupture and ovulation.
  2. **Copper-T IUD Insertion**: Highly effective if inserted within 72–120 hours post-coitus.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Emergency Pill Misconceptions
conceptBreakdown.title: Emergency Pill Misconceptions
conceptBreakdown.content: Emergency contraceptive pills are NOT abortifacients; they cannot terminate an established, implanted pregnancy, and are not intended for routine, regular contraception.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Progestogen-Only Minipills (POPs)
conceptBreakdown.title: Progestogen-Only Minipills (POPs)
conceptBreakdown.content: Minipills contain low-dose progestin without estrogen, making them suitable for lactating mothers without suppressing prolactin-driven milk volume.
